params.body:
## What

`bin/findings-to-issues --apply` mirrored every open finding as a GitHub issue, through the gateway (`issue.open`, control v0.28.1, one record each): #570 to #572 for severity `nu`, #574 to #614 for `deze week`, #616 to #659 for `later`. 88 in total. This writes the numbers back into the files, so the repository and GitHub say the same thing; the file stays the source, the issue is the workbench.

`bin/findings-to-issues` now answers "Elke open bevinding heeft haar issue."

## Worth knowing

The first three took three attempts, and each failure was a missing link rather than a bug in the mirror: the kind was not yet in the grant the VM carried, then the GitHub adapter did not claim the kind it answered (fixed and guarded in abovebeyond-ai/control#87), then the App lacked `Issues: read and write`, which an organisation accepts per installation, the same dance as the Workflows permission on 16 September.

## From here

A pull request that ends a finding writes "Fixes #<n>", sets `status: opgelost`, `opgelost` and `opgelost_in: #<pull request>`; GitHub closes the issue and the file keeps the whole trail.
params.title: Every open finding carries its issue (replaces #573 and #615)
